questions.stem: What changes in CLZ-260 compared with independently keyed Windows VMs?

options.A: Each instance must have a different long-lived role definition
options.B: The VNet is replaced by Terraform state
options.C: The application tier is managed as instances of one shared scale-set model
options.D: All instances become public DNS zones

optionExplanations.A: That is closer to individually keyed servers than this uniform fleet.
optionExplanations.B: State tracks resources but cannot provide networking.
optionExplanations.C: VMSS applies a common compute model to an interchangeable fleet.
optionExplanations.D: The instances remain Windows compute resources.

questions.stem: Which CLZ-260 component encapsulates the Windows VMSS and its load balancer?

options.A: The resource-group output
options.B: The shared windows-iis-vmss module
options.C: The provider version constraint alone
options.D: The admin_username variable

optionExplanations.A: An output exposes a value and does not contain resource definitions.
optionExplanations.B: The root passes context, credentials, sizing, tags, and the web subnet to this module.
optionExplanations.C: A version constraint selects tooling, not a workload module.
optionExplanations.D: That is one module input rather than the module itself.

questions.stem: Why does the root module pass azurerm_subnet.web.id to windows_iis_vmss?

options.A: To place the scale-set NIC configurations in the intended web subnet
options.B: To place the resource group inside the subnet
options.C: To turn the subnet into a Windows administrator credential
options.D: To create one Terraform workspace per subnet address

optionExplanations.A: The shared module uses that ID for its instance network configuration.
optionExplanations.B: Resource groups are logical containers, not subnet residents.
optionExplanations.C: The subnet identity has no credential role.
optionExplanations.D: The reference does not configure Terraform workspaces.

questions.stem: Which root input controls the CLZ-260 VMSS instance capacity?

options.A: admin_cidr
options.B: site_message
options.C: instance_count
options.D: environment

optionExplanations.A: This lesson does not use that input to determine fleet capacity.
optionExplanations.B: The page text does not determine the number of instances.
optionExplanations.C: The root passes this validated value to the module's instances argument.
optionExplanations.D: The environment contributes naming and tags, not the capacity count.

questions.stem: Why does instance_count = 1.5 fail in the lesson?

options.A: The module automatically chooses the next lower integer but then rejects the SKU
options.B: Every scale set must have at least three instances
options.C: The Standard public IP requires an even count
options.D: The capacity validation requires a whole number from one through five

optionExplanations.A: It does not silently round the count.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson permits one through five.
optionExplanations.C: A public frontend does not require even fleet capacity.
optionExplanations.D: Scale-set instance cardinality is an integer.

questions.stem: A learner increases instance_count from two to three. Which evidence should be checked after applying the reviewed plan?

options.A: VMSS capacity is three and the frontend still serves healthy IIS responses
options.B: Only that the input file contains the number three
options.C: Only that the public IP changed
options.D: Only that a new Azure subscription appears

optionExplanations.A: Both desired compute capacity and application delivery should be verified.
optionExplanations.B: Configuration text is not deployed-service evidence.
optionExplanations.C: Scale-out does not require a different frontend IP.
optionExplanations.D: Capacity changes do not create subscriptions.

questions.stem: Does CLZ-260 add instances in response to CPU demand automatically?

options.A: Yes; every VMSS has a default 70-percent CPU rule
options.B: No; the lesson changes capacity deliberately through Terraform inputs
options.C: Yes; the TCP probe creates new instances when busy
options.D: No; because Windows scale sets cannot autoscale

optionExplanations.A: Autoscaling requires a configured policy.
optionExplanations.B: The autoscale setting is introduced in the following lesson.
optionExplanations.C: A probe controls backend health eligibility, not demand-based capacity.
optionExplanations.D: Windows VMSS can autoscale when appropriately configured.

questions.stem: Which input determines the common VM size of the scale-set instances?

options.A: A different each.value.vm_size for every instance
options.B: The current HTTP response length
options.C: vm_size
options.D: The frontend port number

optionExplanations.A: This lesson uses a uniform scale-set model, not the keyed VM map.
optionExplanations.B: Page content does not select the VM SKU.
optionExplanations.C: The root passes one SKU to the shared VMSS model.
optionExplanations.D: Networking ports do not determine compute sizing.

questions.stem: Why should production application data not rely solely on one scale-set instance's local filesystem?

options.A: Instances can be replaced or removed as capacity and models change
options.B: VMSS always converts local files into Private DNS records
options.C: Windows has no filesystem when used in VMSS
options.D: The load balancer stores a copy of every guest disk

optionExplanations.A: Durable application data needs a storage design independent of an interchangeable instance.
optionExplanations.B: No automatic DNS storage conversion occurs.
optionExplanations.C: Windows instances have filesystems.
optionExplanations.D: Load Balancer forwards flows and does not back up disks.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish model policy from capacity control
questions.stem: The module sets upgrade_mode = Manual. What does that setting govern?

options.A: The VM count allowed by the subscription
options.B: The rate at which TCP packets pass through the load balancer
options.C: The number of quiz answers needed for grading
options.D: How existing instances are brought up to date with scale-set model changes

optionExplanations.A: Quota is not defined by upgrade mode.
optionExplanations.B: Upgrade policy does not rate-limit network traffic.
optionExplanations.C: Browser quizzes are unrelated to Azure upgrade policy.
optionExplanations.D: Upgrade policy is separate from the requested number of instances.

questions.stem: The IIS extension has been added to a Manual-policy scale-set model, but older instances do not show it. What should be checked?

options.A: Whether a Role tag contains the extension publisher
options.B: Whether those instances have been explicitly updated to the latest model
options.C: Whether the public frontend has two DNS names
options.D: Whether Terraform formatting adds a semicolon

optionExplanations.A: A tag does not install the extension.
optionExplanations.B: Manual policy does not automatically apply all model additions to existing instances.
optionExplanations.C: DNS labels do not synchronize instance models.
optionExplanations.D: Formatting does not update deployed instances.

questions.learningObjective: Verify guest bootstrap rather than only the model
questions.stem: Which validation best confirms that IIS is usable on the intended VMSS instances?

options.A: Inspect instance extension/model state, probe health, and frontend HTTP responses
options.B: Only list the extension resource in Terraform state
options.C: Only read the module source path
options.D: Only check the admin_username input syntax

optionExplanations.A: Model presence alone is insufficient evidence of successful guest installation.
optionExplanations.B: State records configuration identity rather than the complete guest outcome.
optionExplanations.C: The source path says nothing about runtime health.
optionExplanations.D: A valid username does not demonstrate web serving.

questions.stem: How does the shared module provide explicit Internet egress for private backends?

options.A: Public IPs attached individually to every scale-set NIC
options.B: An inbound RDP NAT mapping on every instance
options.C: An outbound rule on its Standard public load balancer
options.D: The health probe's source address

optionExplanations.A: The module's NIC configuration has only a private subnet association.
optionExplanations.B: No such general egress design is declared by this module.
optionExplanations.C: The pool uses the public frontend for declared SNAT.
optionExplanations.D: Probes are not backend Internet egress.

questions.stem: VMSS capacity equals two, but the frontend times out. What should the learner investigate?

options.A: Increase the maximum map key length
options.B: Instance bootstrap, model readiness, NSG access, and health probes
options.C: Assume the Azure capacity report is automatically an HTTP success
options.D: Publish the administrator password so the frontend can authenticate clients

optionExplanations.A: This lesson does not use map key length for guest readiness.
optionExplanations.B: A correct instance count does not guarantee an application listener is ready.
optionExplanations.C: Control-plane capacity and data-plane delivery are separate.
optionExplanations.D: The HTTP teaching path does not require publishing guest credentials.

questions.stem: The module's TCP probe on port 80 is healthy. Which assertion is still too strong?

options.A: The backend accepts TCP on the configured probe port
options.B: The probe configuration is targeting port 80
options.C: The healthy backend can receive new eligible load-balanced flows
options.D: All business dependencies and page content are correct

optionExplanations.A: That is what a successful TCP probe supports.
optionExplanations.B: That is the module's declared port.
optionExplanations.C: Probe health supports eligibility for those flows.
optionExplanations.D: A TCP connection check does not inspect application semantics.

questions.stem: How should a learner assess quota for instance_count = 4?

options.A: Check only that one instance can be created
options.B: Check the selected VM size's regional quota and capacity for four instances
options.C: Multiply only the number of public frontend IPs
options.D: Assume a valid size string reserves four instances

optionExplanations.A: One available instance does not establish capacity for four.
optionExplanations.B: The full requested fleet must fit the target subscription and region.
optionExplanations.C: The compute quota concerns VM instances and their sizes.
optionExplanations.D: Input syntax does not reserve Azure capacity.

questions.stem: Why should the default small instance_count remain small during manual-scaling practice?

options.A: Terraform charges a fee for every integer in the input
options.B: The page message is priced per character
options.C: The resource-group name costs more when capacity increases
options.D: Each additional running VMSS instance adds compute and managed-disk cost

optionExplanations.A: The input number itself is not billable.
optionExplanations.B: Page text length is not the fleet's main cost driver.
optionExplanations.C: Group naming does not incur per-instance charges.
optionExplanations.D: Manual capacity is a direct lab cost driver.

questions.stem: What does vmss_load_balancer_url expose?

options.A: The private IP of the first instance's RDP listener
options.B: A signed URL containing the administrator password
options.C: The HTTP URL of the module-created public load balancer
options.D: The Terraform remote-state storage key

optionExplanations.A: That is not the module's output.
optionExplanations.B: The endpoint does not need to embed that secret.
optionExplanations.C: The root forwards the module's load_balancer_url output.
optionExplanations.D: This module output is a web endpoint, not backend configuration.

questions.stem: Why is selecting the Windows Server 2022 platform image alone not enough to serve the lesson page?

options.A: The IIS extension separately installs the web role and writes the page
options.B: The Standard load balancer stores index.html itself
options.C: VMSS only supports Linux web pages
options.D: The public IP is the operating-system installer

optionExplanations.A: The application configuration is distinct from the base operating system.
optionExplanations.B: Content is served by guest IIS.
optionExplanations.C: This module deploys Windows instances.
optionExplanations.D: Public IP provisioning does not install IIS.

questions.stem: The module base64-encodes site_message before its PowerShell command decodes it. Why is that helpful?

options.A: It encrypts an administrator password against every reader
options.B: It causes the VMSS to autoscale on message length
options.C: It replaces the need for jsonencode on extension settings
options.D: It transports the page text through the nested command-string quoting safely

optionExplanations.A: Base64 is encoding, not encryption.
optionExplanations.B: Text encoding does not control capacity.
optionExplanations.C: The settings still require valid JSON.
optionExplanations.D: The decoded text is then written into the intended web file.

questions.stem: The module admin_password variable is sensitive. What still needs protection?

options.A: The public page message as if it were always a password
options.B: Only the CSS file
options.C: Terraform state and any explicit secret artifacts
options.D: Nothing after the module has received the password

optionExplanations.A: The page message is intended nonsecret lesson content.
optionExplanations.B: CSS is not the VM administrator credential store.
optionExplanations.C: Sensitive marking limits display but does not erase stored credentials.
optionExplanations.D: The password can remain in Terraform-managed values.

questions.stem: A learner passes the VNet's address prefix string as subnet_id. Why is that wrong?

options.A: The module expects the subnet's Azure resource ID
options.B: A subnet prefix is valid only in a Role tag
options.C: The module expects the administrator password for subnet_id
options.D: The module automatically creates a subnet from any string

optionExplanations.A: The NIC configuration requires a resource identity, not an IP range.
optionExplanations.B: Prefixes can define networks, but are not resource IDs.
optionExplanations.C: Credentials and subnet identities are separate inputs.
optionExplanations.D: It consumes an existing declared subnet rather than inferring one.

questions.learningObjective: Review a VM size model change
questions.stem: The exercise changes only vm_size in a disposable plan. What should be reviewed?

options.A: Only the page's font size
options.B: The proposed scale-set model update and consequences for existing instances
options.C: Only whether Terraform renamed the lesson folder
options.D: Only the frontend port, because it encodes the SKU

optionExplanations.A: CSS is unrelated to compute SKU.
optionExplanations.B: SKU changes affect the model and may require explicit instance updates under Manual policy.
optionExplanations.C: A size input does not rename the local folder.
optionExplanations.D: The port does not encode compute size.

questions.stem: Which improvement fits the lesson's production guidance for fleet upgrades?

options.A: Change all instances at once without health checks
options.B: Use a shared browser cookie as the upgrade policy
options.C: Versioned images, tested rolling rollout, and application health monitoring
options.D: Keep every obsolete model indefinitely and never inspect instances

optionExplanations.A: That risks simultaneous unavailability.
optionExplanations.B: Browser state cannot orchestrate Azure instance upgrades.
optionExplanations.C: Controlled upgrades reduce unmanaged instance drift and service disruption.
optionExplanations.D: Unreviewed drift is not a sound production rollout.

questions.stem: New scale-set instances have been created but are not yet eligible for frontend traffic. Which explanation is plausible?

options.A: Every new instance must wait for the public IP to change
options.B: Guest bootstrap and probe readiness may lag instance provisioning
options.C: Terraform plan is continuously serving HTTP requests
options.D: The public IP must be assigned directly to each guest first

optionExplanations.A: The frontend address can remain stable during scale-out.
optionExplanations.B: Application warm-up is a separate stage after compute creation.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform is a deployment tool, not the web server.
optionExplanations.D: The pool is intended to serve private backend NICs.

questions.stem: Where does CLZ-260 attach the web NSG in its root configuration?

options.A: Only to the Terraform working directory
options.B: To the administrator password output
options.C: To a Bastion subnet that the module creates
options.D: To the web subnet used by the VMSS

optionExplanations.A: Azure NSGs attach to network resources, not local directories.
optionExplanations.B: An output is not a network policy attachment point.
optionExplanations.C: The module does not create a Bastion subnet.
optionExplanations.D: The subnet association applies the declared policy to that network tier.

questions.stem: Why should a learner not delete the Terraform state file as a substitute for VMSS cleanup?

options.A: It can leave the VMSS, disks, and frontend resources running without tracking
options.B: State deletion guarantees the VMSS stops immediately
options.C: State is the load balancer's CPU controller
options.D: State deletion always preserves safe resource ownership

optionExplanations.A: Deleting metadata does not call Azure deletion APIs.
optionExplanations.B: That is not its effect.
optionExplanations.C: State is deployment tracking, not an autoscale controller.
optionExplanations.D: It instead weakens the ability to track ownership.

questions.stem: Which pair most directly supports CLZ-260's expected outcome?

options.A: Azure reports the requested capacity and HTTP returns the intended IIS response
options.B: A matching local folder name and a successful terraform fmt
options.C: A saved password and a resource-group Project tag
options.D: A public IP address and an empty browser history

optionExplanations.A: One verifies compute state; the other exercises web delivery.
optionExplanations.B: These do not prove deployed capacity or application readiness.
optionExplanations.C: Credentials and tags do not demonstrate service health.
optionExplanations.D: Neither pair checks the intended fleet count and endpoint.

questions.stem: Which resources must the final documented cleanup remove?

options.A: Only the HTTP page file in one guest
options.B: Only the local tfvars example
options.C: Only the quiz answers for CLZ-260
options.D: The VMSS instances, load balancer, public IP, and supporting lesson network

optionExplanations.A: That leaves the Azure fleet and network resources.
optionExplanations.B: Deleting an example does not remove deployed infrastructure.
optionExplanations.C: Browser progress is independent of Azure resource cleanup.
optionExplanations.D: Destroy should remove the entire managed lab footprint.

questions.stem: What is the preferred sequence for a capacity change in CLZ-260?

options.A: Edit the input and assume Azure detects the file automatically
options.B: Edit the validated input, create and inspect a plan, apply it, and verify Azure capacity and HTTP
options.C: Remove state locking and submit multiple simultaneous applies
options.D: Only restart one guest without updating Terraform's desired capacity

optionExplanations.A: Azure does not watch local Terraform files for automatic apply.
optionExplanations.B: The sequence connects intent, review, execution, and evidence.
optionExplanations.C: Concurrent uncoordinated changes threaten state consistency.
optionExplanations.D: A guest restart does not make a capacity change.
